messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: QR trick with cauchy pooling?
parts:
Hi folks,

When doing exploratory multiple regression, I've taken to pooling using a cauchy(0,1) prior on the pooling parameter (after scaling outcomes & predictors to have mean of 0 and sd of 1). I noticed the new section in the manual on the QR trick, so I thought I'd see how it fares with pooled regression. It seems to be emulate the non-QR result when the pooling parameter has a normal(0,1) prior in both variants, but when a cauchy is used, the non-QR seems to better identify "real" effects that are added while the QR variant maintains the result as when a normal(0,1) is used. 


Attached are the two models (non-QR & QR) and an R script to generate/evaluate/plot some fake data.

Here's coefficient plot for the non-QR version:



And here's the QR version:




Now, obviously if I were to see this latter plot, I wouldn't give much credibility to the three blue "excludes zero" points that are in the cluster of "doesn't exclude zero" points, but it would be nice for the QR version to have the same result. So is there a way to set the pooling prior in the QR version to emulate a cauchy pooling prior in the non-QR version?

Mike


--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] QR trick with cauchy pooling?
parts:
You’re specifying a different model so the different results are
not unexpected. To get an equivalent model you have to
reconstruct the untransformed slopes in transformed parameters
and then put a prior on those. You will get a Jacobian warning,
but the transformation is linear so you can ignore it.

You also want to avoid computing the inverse directly. Do
something like

beta = mdivide_right_tri_low(beta_tilde', R')';

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] QR trick with cauchy pooling?
parts:
Ah, I always forget that it's ok to have something on the left hand side of an "=" in transformed parameters but also on the left hand side of an "~" in the model. (Which I'll admit is another argument for the use of "target +=" rather than my otherwise preferred "~")

So yes, this does achieve the assertion of a cauchy prior on the coefficients as in the non-QR version. 

Just curious: in the non-QR version I can improve sampling by reparameterizing the cauchy as described on pg 322 of the manual (v2.14.0); is this reparamerterization not possible with the QR version?

That is, if I have the following in the non-QR version:

  ...
  parameters{
    vector[nX] coefs ;
    ... 
  }
  model{
    coefs ~ cauchy(0,1) ;
    ...
  }

I can improve sampling by doing:

  ...
  parameters{
    vector<lower=-pi()/2,upper=pi()/2>[nX] coefs_unif ;
    ... 
  }
  transformed parameters{
    vector[nX] coefs ;
    coefs = tan(coefs_unif) ;
  }
  model{
    ...
  }


But if I have my QR version as:

  ...
  model{
    vector[nX] theta ;
    ...
  }
  transformed parameters{
    vector[nX] coefs ;
    coefs = R_ast_inverse * theta ;
  }
  model{
    coefs ~ cauchy(0,1) ;
    ...
  }

I'm not sure how to apply the cauchy reparameterization since coefs is already on the left hand side of an "=". Thoughts?

Mike
